## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Start a week or two in advance by spraying all bolts that will be removed with PB Blast.
2. Remove the white plastic caps covering four bolt heads inside the truck using a small chisel and hammer.
3. Spray the exposed bolt heads under those caps with PB Blast.
4. [Partial] Lift up slightly on each side of the cab to remove the carpet partially, exposing the front mounts.
5. Take off the plastic kick rails by removing their screws.
6. [Partial] Remove the interior panel located near the front mounts.
7. [Partial] Locate and identify the four exterior body mount positions: two under the front rocker panels, one between the doors on the rear rocker panel, and one in front of the rear wheels.
8. Spray all identified body mount bolts thoroughly with PB Blast.
9. Spray the steering shaft bolts at both the top and bottom locations with PB Blast.
10. On lift day, spray all previously treated bolts again with fresh PB Blast.
11. Remove the four main bumper mounting bolts located in front of the radiator.
12. Take off the two smaller side bumper bolts situated behind the marker lights.
13. Disconnect the cables for the marker lights while accessing them from inside the bumper area.
14. [Partial] Slide out the rear bumper brackets and remove the six nuts holding the rear bumper on each side.
15. [Partial] Twist and pull straight to remove the license plate light bulbs without breaking their wires.
16. Tie off the steering wheel with rope so it cannot turn freely.
17. Loosen but do not fully remove the bolts on the steering shaft to allow for extension during lifting.
18. Undo the clip securing the heater core hoses inside the engine compartment.
19. Remove the two bolts holding the drive shaft safety loop and slide the loop out of the way.
20. [Partial] Slide the power steering reservoir out of its bracket by cutting 2 inches off a side and welding it back together if necessary.
21. Loosen the hose clamps on the intake manifold.
22. [Partial] Remove the screws securing the brake line bracket to the frame, relocating them if needed with a tap set.
23. [Partial] Unclip and remove the lower half of the cooling fan shroud from behind the radiator.
24. [Partial] Cut a notch in the transfer case shifter area to allow for full range of movement into 4LO.
25. Spray all body mount bolts again generously with PB Blast just before removal.
26. Lift one side of the vehicle using jacks placed on railroad ties under the body rather than the frame.
27. Place lift pucks underneath each bolt location as the body rises to create clearance.
28. Finger-tighten the removed bolts back into place, applying a bit of red lock tite before seating them.
29. Lift and repeat the puck placement and finger-tightening process on the opposite side of the vehicle.
30. Torque the passenger side (P) bolts in this specific order: P1, D3, P4, D1, P3, D5, P2, then finish with P5.
31. [Partial] [Unverified value] Set the torque for positions 7 and 9 (P2 and P5) to between 14-18 ft.lbs.
32. [Partial] [Unverified value] Torque position 6 (D5) to between 14-18 ft.lbs as well since it shares that spec group with P2, D3, etc. based on the guide's grouping logic for the remaining bolts.
33. [Partial] [Unverified value] Set the torque for positions 2 and 4 (D3 and D1) to between 22-31 ft.lbs.
34. [Partial] [Unverified value] Torque position 5 (P3) to between 22-31 ft.lbs as part of that middle group.
35. [Partial] Finally, torque positions 8 and 10 (D4 and D2) using the remaining spec from the final pair listed in the guide's sequence.

_Procedure reported by [t1698]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/diy-2-body-lift.328/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1698] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Drain the radiator or loosen both upper and lower hose clamps to relieve pressure.
2. [Partial] Loosen the hoses connecting to the heater core on the firewall, unclipping them from brackets if necessary.
3. [Partial] Remove bolts holding the airbox down; move the bracket until it rests against the intake hose before tightening.
4. Unbolt brake lines and EVAP lines attached to the frame behind a shield near the front passenger wheel.
5. Unbolt the emergency brake cable bracket mounted on the driver side frame rail.
6. Loosen but do not remove both bolts connecting the steering shaft (one near firewall, one by gearbox).
7. Turn the steering wheel so both loosened bolts point upward to prevent binding during lift.
8. Tie off or secure the steering wheel in position using a ratchet with long extensions if needed.
9. Lift each side of the vehicle slowly while watching for stretched hoses, wires, and rubbing brake lines.
10. Unclip wiring harnesses from brackets that restrict travel to allow full suspension movement.
11. Slide the loose section of the steering shaft between its two bolts so both ends have maximum grip.
12. [Partial] Reconnect all disconnected lines and secure any popped-out plastic clips with zip ties or new hose.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1046] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Find a flat surface and ensure all tires are properly inflated.
2. Measure from the ground to the bottom of each door near its wheel well and write down the numbers.
3. [Partial] Locate the rear shackles, torsion bar adjuster bolts, and nuts on both sides.
4. [Partial] Spray PB Blaster or Freeze Off onto the shackle hardware to prevent rust welding.
5. [Partial] Spray the top nut head of each front torsion bar adjuster bolt with chemical penetrant.
6. Raise the vehicle slightly under the front differential using a jack while keeping tires on the ground.
7. Loosen the top locking nut on one side's front torsion bar just enough to move freely.
8. Hold the bottom adjusting nut in place with an open-end wrench.
9. Turn the bolt head clockwise underneath the vehicle until there is about 0.5-0.75 inch of gap between the upper control arm and bump stop.
10. Repeat this adjustment process on the other side to match the first one.
11. [Partial] Tighten both lock nuts securely without fully locking them down yet.

</details>

## Specifications

- **Adjustable shackle max height**: 2 1/8" [t1046] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Bottom leaf thickness (overload)**: 1.5 inch [t1922] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Bump stop gap target**: 0.5-0.75 inches [t1046] ([Unverified] single report)
- **First and last mount torque**: 23-32 ft.lbs. [t1698] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Front lift estimate**: ~1.5 inches [t1046] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Rear AAL Lift Height**: 2.5 inches [t1922] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Rear leaf spring lift (AAL)**: 2.5 inches [t1922] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Rear shackle length (typical)**: ~1.5 inches [t1046] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Second and third mount torque**: 22-31 ft.lbs. [t1698] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Total rear lift potential (AAL + Shackle)**: 2.25 to 2.50 inches [t1922] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- Use shims made from paint stirring sticks taped together to measure small gaps. [t1046]
- [Partial] Apply penetrating oil like PB Blaster or Freeze Off to hardware a week before lifting to prevent rust welding. [t1046]
- [Partial] Use this method if there is no room for the bolt head to thread into the nut anymore. [t1046]
- [Partial] Apply when you have reached bump stop limits but need more range of motion on the lever arm. [t1046]
- Use an adjustable rear shackle if you want to fine-tune lift height after adjusting the front torsion bars. [t1046]
- Watch the bump stop gap to estimate how much free front end lift you have gained. [t1046]
- Ensure tires are properly inflated and have similar tread height before taking preliminary measurements. [t1046]
- Work on a flat surface like an evenly laid garage floor for accuracy. [t1046]
- Use a scissor jack between the frame and leaf spring to flex the spring down if longer shackles don't fit at the top. [t1046]
- [Partial] Disconnect shock absorbers or use upgraded 3-inch shocks to avoid needing extra leverage for long shackles. [t1046]
- [Partial] A high-lift farm jack works well to support both sides while keeping a tire on during installation. [t1046]
- [Partial] Parts cost approximately $80 for the complete set. [t1045]
- [Partial] A method known as 're-indexing' for fine-tuning suspension geometry. [t1045]
- Known as 'PML' or Poor Man's Lift; uses simple spacer blocks. [t1045]
- [Partial] Common fix for high-clearance vehicles where mud splashes into diffs. [t1045]
- [Partial] A 'homebrew' or eBay solution allows wading deeper than stock height. [t1045]
- [Partial] Uses Hella FF75 units mentioned in related threads. [t1045]
- Add nylon or rubber washers if retaining the drive shaft safety loop. [t1483]
- Use extra spacers rather than hunting for perfectly length-matched bolts to avoid bottoming out. [t1483]
- Consider cutting 2-inch pucks in half to create a custom 1-inch lift. [t1483]
- Loosen bolts on the opposite side before fully removing them from one side to prevent extra stress. [t1698]
- [Partial] Use a very long extension socket for reaching steering shaft bolts if available. [t1698]
- [Partial] Cut and weld 2 inches off the power steering reservoir bracket height to clear suspension travel. [t1698]
- Spray body bolts with PB Blaster a few days ahead of time. [t1698]
- [Partial] Loosen upper radiator hose before lifting, then tighten and top off coolant afterward. [t1698]
- Use 3/8" power steering hose slit open to wrap around brake lines where they rub against other parts. [t1698]
- [Partial] Zip tie popped-out plastic clips on wiring harnesses or rubbing brake lines. [t1698]
- The heavy-duty springs provide a slight lift even on stock setups. [t1941]
- Axle tube diameter helps balance the weight of rear bumpers and tire carriers. [t1941]
- [Partial] Consider swapping rear shocks for longer travel Bilsteins (like 4600 or 7100 series) to handle increased flex. [t1922]
- [Partial] Extend brake lines if using revolver shackles, though stock length may suffice in the front. [t1922]
- Loosen opposite bolts first to prevent body shifting before removing hardware. [t1698]
- Use a 2x2 square steel piece for the front bumper mount and drill holes to align with existing mounts. [t1698]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Over-tightening rear lug nuts, which can tear the metal of the tire sidewall or ruin the tire iron. [t1046]
- [Partial] Forgetting that the rear-most mount points use longer bolts into nuts welded to the frame. [t1483]
- [Partial] Assuming all 10-12 mounting bolts are identical lengths without checking specific locations. [t1483]
- [Partial] Torquing all bolts on one entire side down at once before balancing with the other side. [t1698]
- [Partial] Forgetting the heater core hoses and unclipping them from brackets before lifting. [t1698]
- [Partial] Bolted down the airbox in its original position, making it hard to hook up the intake hose. [t1698]
- [Partial] Yanking radiator shroud until broken instead of figuring out how to unclip it. [t1698]
